subject: Post-signature implementation: rollout & canary MAP for Finovate Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@finovatehealth.com>, Sarah Lewis <s.lewis@finovatehealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Post-signature implementation MAP and proposed rollout window

Hi Paul / Sarah,

Congrats again on the signed SOW — excited to get Finovate Health onto Redwood Dedicated. Attached is a first-draft Post-Signature MAP that embeds the implementation plan we discussed (rollout phases, canary plan, data migration window, and training cadence). Key highlights in this email:

- Week 0 (prep): account provisioning, network allowlists, KMS/HSM integration checklist (security team will validate).
- Week 1 (staging canary): deploy model + mirror traffic at 5-10% for two rolling days. Success criteria: p95 latency < 220ms, no more than 0.2% inference errors, and parity on top-1 intent for curated eval set.
- Week 2 (pilot rollout): escalate to 30% traffic with telemetry + rollback triggers in place.
- Week 3 (full cutover): migrate remaining traffic; final validation and ops handoff.
- Training: 2 sessions for Ops (runbook + failover) and 1 session for Product with recorded artifacts.

Please review the attached MAP (Finovate-Post-Signature-MAP-v1.pdf) and the migration checklist (finovate-migration-checklist.xlsx). I put a DocuSign link for SOW execution in related_links; once we have signed dates we'll lock the deployment windows.

Questions for you:
1) Can you confirm preferred blackout windows for production migration?
2) Who on your side will own the traffic-mirroring verification?
3) Any org-level compliance checks we should schedule with your security lead during Week 0?

If these look good, propose we start staging canary the week of Mar 9.

Thanks,

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0134

Thanks Marissa — this looks comprehensive and aligned with our earlier discussion. A few clarifications from our side:

- Blackout windows: avoid weekdays 08:00-10:00 PT (high traffic) and 12:00-13:00 PT (batch jobs). After-hours (20:00-23:00 PT) or weekends preferred.
- Traffic mirroring: I'll own verification but will have Sarah run daily checks during the canary.
- Compliance: I'll loop in our security lead (CC'd) if we need deeper evidence; for now basic KMS proof of concept is fine.

Two asks:
1) Can you tighten the staging canary to a single 48-hour window (two consecutive days) rather than two non-consecutive days?
2) Provide an ops runbook draft for the rollback trigger conditions (we want clear decision points).

I'll also route the SOW for signatures today — I see the DocuSign link. If we sign this week, we can target the Mar 9 staging date.

—Paul

Thanks — yes, we can do the 48-hour consecutive canary. Updated plan below and attached a one-page ops runbook draft in the MAP PDF:

- Staging Canary: 48 consecutive hours at 5-10% mirror traffic, continuous telemetry, daily sync calls at 09:00 PT.
- Rollback triggers (high level):
  • sustained p95 latency > 300ms for > 10 minutes
  • error rate > 0.5% for any 15-minute window
  • model quality regression > 2% on the curated eval set over 1 hour

I'll update the MAP and push a new version to the Drive link (see related_links). If DocuSign completes today we'll lock the Mar 9 canary.

Next steps for you: confirm the after-hours window you prefer (Fri night vs Sat night), and who on your security team should be the single point of contact for KMS validation.

Thanks,

Marissa
